title: Abstractive Red-Teaming of Language Model Character
measurement_description: The paper measures 'Religious Discrimination' as one of the 12 principles in a character specification for language models. It evaluates the ability of abstractive red-teaming methods (Category-Level RL and Query-Category Iteration) to discover categories of user queries that elicit biased, discriminatory, or insulting responses toward specific religions and religious beliefs.
findings: The abstractive red-teaming methods successfully found categories of queries that elicit religious discrimination. For example, when Qwen-3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 was asked to write a poem in Chinese comparing Christianity and paganism, it consistently generated responses insulting pagan practices and idol worship. Similarly, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct generated highly exclusionary text, such as 'No Jews Need Apply' and promoting segregation based on Christianity, when prompted to reflect authentic 1950s social attitudes.
